## WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) Benefits 
**What is WIC?**
- The California Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) program is a food and nutrition program for growing families. You can get help with nutrition education, breastfeeding and chestfeeding support, benefits to buy healthy foods, and referrals to health care and other community services. 

**Eligibility:**
You may qualify if you: 
- Are pregnant, breastfeeding or just had a baby or recent pregnancy loss in the last 6 months **or** have a child or care for a child under 5 years old **and**
- have low to medium income (earn less than 185% of the federal poverty level) or recieve Medi-Cal, CalWORKS, or CalFresh **and**
- live in California

Important: only staff at your local WIC can officially confirm if you qualify or not.

Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

Rent or mortgage help: 
Calling 2-1-1 in California is the best way to find help to pay your rent, mortagage, utilities bills to stay in your home. Call to speak to someone right away. They will ask you a few questions about your current living situation, any income, any children or dependents who live with you. First, you should talk with your landlord if you rent or lender if you have a mortgage to discuss your situation. There may be options like payment plans that could help you stay in your home. Types of Benefits: you can get up to a $19 monthly discount for flat rate service or cell phone service, a service connection discount $39, and certain taxes and user fees are made free

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $29,187 for a household of 2). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc.

Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. The most financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 250% of the federal poverty level ($29,187 to $52,875 for a tax household of 2), but even individuals making up to 400% of the federal poverty level could get help. If you are already recieving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. 
Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 

## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

## Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan):

- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps:

    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed.

- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you.

How much you get is related to how much you were earning before you lost your job - the more you were making, the more likely that you could get the max weekly amount of $450. 

Unemployment Insurance 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

California has a lot of support both in helping you find a job again and in getting some income every week until you find new work. They do not connect you to other benefits directly, but I can give you some examples of what else is out there. If you want any more information on any of these, just let me know: 

Call 2-1-1, they are a 24/7 available help line to get you connected to support in California for food, housing, healthcare, and more. 

Unemployment Insurance: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria.

For maternal health resources, you also have support available:

Covering phone bills:

Types of Benefits: you can get up to a $19 monthly discount for flat rate service or cell phone service, a service connection discount $39, and certain taxes and user fees are made free 
Eligibility: You can qualify two ways. For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. 

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $36,777 for a household of 3). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. 

Using and Keeping your coverage:

It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you apply and get approved as a reminder. 

## Covered California Details
Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. The most financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 250% of the federal poverty level ($36,777 to $66,625 for a tax household of 3), but even individuals making up to 400% of the federal poverty level could get help.If you are already receiving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Gathering these documents ahead of time can make the application process go faster: 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you such as the following: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). You must report any changes in your life situation to (for example, address, family size, income) within 30 days. 
Renewal is in the fall of each year and goes to the end of the calendar year. You'll get notified by Covered California when it's time. 

## COBRA insurance 
COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator.

There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan):

- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you.

I'm so sorry to hear you've lost your job. This is a scary time but know you're not alone. California has many resources available to help folks who fall on hard times. 

It's normal to feel anxious or down after losing a job. If you want to talk to someone, you can call 988 any time, 24/7 for free to speak with a caring counselor: https://988lifeline.org/ 

You can also call 2-1-1, any time for free help getting connected to resources in your area that can help you with food, healthcare, childcare, and more. 

If you want to learn more about programs out there to help specific needs you have, let me know and I can provide more information. Some help options below specifically related to job loss and finding a new job: 

Unemployment Benefits can help make ends meet while you keep looking for a new job: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

California also offers a lot of options finding a new job: 
- Workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. Yes, you might be able to get both. Make sure to include the income you get from unemployment benefits and severance when you apply for Medi-Cal. As long as you still meet Medi-Cal income requirements, you can get both. 

Here's more information: 

Unemployment Benefits can help make ends meet while you keep looking for a new job: 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. Since the gig work would be part time while you find a full time role, you would likely be eligible for less money in unemployment. And you would need to explain that the part time gig work is only temporary until you find full time work. Applying is the best way to know if you're eligible or not.  
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.
Request for Identity Verification (DE 1326C): If you applied by phone, fax, or mail (or we can’t immediately verify your identity), you’ll receive this form. Visit Respond to Your Request for Identity Verification to learn how to avoid further delays.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. 

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $21,597 for a household of 1). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California (if your part-time gig work puts you over Medi-Cal income limits). 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up. 
- If anything changes in your situation like moving, income amount, number of people in your home, pregnancy, or marital status, you need to update your application within 10 days. 
- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you apply and get approved as a reminder.

- CalFresh and UI Benefits and severance: Yes you can still get CalFresh while getting UI benefits but the amount of money can't go over CalFresh income limits. Severance would count as part of your income from the last 30 days and may affect your first month of CalFresh benefits.

- If you need food now, you can go to your local county food bank or call first to see if you qualify for help:  https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks

Unemployment Benefits can help make ends meet while you keep looking for a new job: 
- When you move, just make sure to update your address in personal information. As long as you are still in California, it shouldn't impact your unemployment benefits. 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from $40 to $450 each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
--Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)

--Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively).

Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. Details below: 
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Claim Filed (DE 1101CLMT): This is a summary of your claim information. It explains how to correct any errors to avoid payment delays.
Employment Development Department Customer Account Number Notification (DE 5614): This has your EDD Customer Account Number (EDDCAN) to register in UI Online, after you visit myEDD. The EDDCAN also helps verify your account if you speak with an EDD representative. Don’t lose it.
Notice of Unemployment Insurance Award (DE 429Z): This form explains what benefits you can expect, and how to avoid payment delays. If any information is wrong, follow the instructions and appeal in writing within 30 days to avoid payment delays.
Unemployment Insurance Benefits: What You Need to Know (DE 1275B): This provides you a link to a document that explains how you can avoid payment delays by accurately certifying for benefits every two weeks.
Continued Claim (DE 4581): You can use this form to certify by paper, but the process is much slower. Save time and do it online at myEDD or by phone. You’ll certify for benefits every two weeks.

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.", 
"## How to get COBRA coverage

When a qualifying life event happens, you or your employer will notify the health plan. The plan will send an election notice that you will have 60 days to respond to. If you elect to take COBRA coverage, your employer may pay a portion of or the full amount of your insurance premium.
- Contact your employer’s health insurance plan administrator with questions about COBRA, including:
- If you currently have COBRA coverage
- When your COBRA coverage will begin
- How long the coverage may last"],

- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

## Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan): 
After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) and ACA Marketplace (Covered California), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you. 

For help with paying for or finding child care, California has options. 

## CalWORKS Child Care Benefits 
What is it? 
- Get assistance paying for child care with a provider of your choice. 
- Child care is available for children through age 12 and for exceptional needs and severely disabled children up to age 21 

Eligibility: 
- If you currently get or previously got CalWORKs cash aid, and are currently employed or participating in a county approved Welfare-to-Work program you may be eligible 

How to apply: 
- Contact your local county welfare department to apply and learn more. If you give me your county information, I can look up your local agency for you?

## Local Child Care Resource and Referral Agency (R&R) 
What is it?
- Local Child Care Resource and Referral programs keep a list of child care providers and provides resources and information for parents looking for child care 
- Go to their website here: https://rrnetwork.org/family-services/find-child-care or call 1-800-KIDS-793 for help 

## County Alternative Payment Program (APP) 
You can reach out to community based organizations in your county to learn about alternative payment programs to help make child care affordable. Look here for more information: https://www.cappaonline.com/aps-in-california

COBRA is another temporary option for health coverage. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: 
- Termination of reduction in employee hours 
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan

- A qualifying life event must occur

["## Learn about COBRA insurance and how to get coverage

- COBRA, the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act, lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.", 
"## How does COBRA insurance work?

- COBRA applies to most private sector businesses with 20 or more employees. It requires an employer's group health insurance plan to continue after qualifying life events. These include:
- Termination or a reduction of a covered employee's hours
- Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of a covered employee
- Medicare eligibility for a covered employee
- Loss of a child's or dependent's health insurance coverage under the plan
- Qualified beneficiaries under COBRA include:
- An employee
- Spouse
- Former spouses
- Dependent children
- The amount of time COBRA benefits last depends on the qualifying life event you experience. In some cases, it may be for 36 months. If your hours were reduced or your job was terminated, you can receive COBRA benefits for 18 months.", 
"## Find out if you are eligible for COBRA

- COBRA eligibility has three basic requirements that must be met for you to get a continuation of coverage:
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA.
- A qualifying event must occur.
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for that event.",
